Arrow Functions
Arrow functions is a short syntax for writing function expressions.

You don't need the function keyword, the return keyword, or the
curly brackets.
let myFunction = function(a, b) {return a * b}
blocks.caption: Before Arrow:

blocks.text: let myFunction = (a, b) => a * b;
blocks.caption: With Arrow

blocks.text:
Arrow functions do not have their own this.
They are not well suited for defining object methods.
Arrow functions are not hoisted. They must be defined before they are used.

You can only omit the return keyword and the curly brackets if the function is a single
statement. Because of this, it might be a good habit to always keep them:

blocks.text: The For/Of Loop

The JavaScript for/of statement loops
through the values of iterable objects.

for/of lets you loop over data structures
that are iterable such as Arrays, Strings, Maps, NodeLists, and more.
The for/of loop has the following syntax:

variable - For every iteration the value of the next property is
assigned to the variable. Variable can be declared with
const, let, or var.
iterable - An object that has iterable properties.

JavaScript Maps
A Map is an object that stores key-value pairs, similar to objects, but with differences:

items:
Keys can be of any data type (objects, functions, primitive values),
unlike plain objects where keys are strings.
Maintains the original insertion order of keys.

blocks.text: Being able to use an Object as a key is an important Map feature.

blocks.caption: Example

JavaScript Sets
A Set is an object that stores unique values of any type (primitive values, functions, objects).
A Set can only contain unique values. An attempt to add a duplicate value will be ignored.

JavaScript Promises

A JavaScript Promise is an object representing the completion or failure of an asynchronous
operation and its values.

It is a placeholder for a value that may not yet be available,
providing a structured way to handle asynchronous code.

The Symbol Type
A JavaScript Symbol is a primitive data type just like Number, String, or Boolean.
It represents a unique "hidden" identifier that no other code can accidentally access.

For instance, if different coders want to add a person.id property to a person object belonging to a third-party code,
they could mix each others values.
Using Symbol() to create a unique identifiers, solves this problem:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
Symbols are always unique.
If you create two symbols with the same description they will have different values:

Symbol("id") == Symbol("id"); // false

blocks.text: String.includes()

The includes() method returns true if a string contains a specified value,
otherwise false:

let text = "Hello world, welcome to the universe.";

text.includes("world")    // Returns true
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: String.startsWith()

The startsWith() method returns true
if a string begins with a specified value, otherwise false:

let text = "Hello world, welcome to the universe.";

text.startsWith("Hello")   // Returns true
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: String.endsWith()

The endsWith() method returns true
if a string ends with a specified value, otherwise false:

var text = "John Doe";

text.endsWith("Doe")    // Returns true
blocks.caption: Example

New Math Methods
ES6 added the following methods to the Math object:
The Math.trunc() Method
Math.trunc(x) returns the integer part of x:

Math.trunc(4.9);    // returns 4

Math.trunc(4.7);    // returns 4

Math.trunc(4.4);    // returns 4

Math.trunc(4.2);    // returns 4

Math.trunc(-4.2);    // returns -4
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Math.sign() Method
Math.sign(x) returns -1, 0, or 1 (if x is negative, null or positive):

Math.sign(-4);    // returns -1

Math.sign(0);    // returns 0

Math.sign(4);    // returns 1
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Math.cbrt() Method
Math.cbrt(x) returns the cube root of x:

Math.cbrt(8);    // returns 2

Math.cbrt(64);    // returns 4

Math.cbrt(125);    // returns 5
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Math.log2() Method
Math.log2(x) returns the base 2 logarithm of x:
Math.log2(2);    // returns 1
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Math.log10() Method
Math.log10(x) returns the base 10 logarithm of x:
Math.log10(10);    // returns 1
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Number.isInteger() Method
The Number.isInteger() method returns true if the argument is an integer.

Number.isInteger(10);        // returns true

Number.isInteger(10.5);      // returns false
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Number.isSafeInteger() Method
A safe integer is an integer that can be exactly represented as a double precision number.
The Number.isSafeInteger() method returns true if the argument is a safe integer.

Number.isSafeInteger(10);    // returns true

Number.isSafeInteger(12345678901234567890);  // returns false
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: New Global Methods
ES6 added 2 new global number methods:
The isFinite() Method
The global isFinite() method returns false if the argument is Infinity or NaN.
Otherwise it returns true:

isFinite(10/0);       // returns false

isFinite(10/1);       // returns true
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The isNaN() Method
The global isNaN() method returns true if the argument is NaN. Otherwise it returns false:
isNaN("Hello");       // returns true
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: RegExp u Modifier

blocks.caption: Examples
Examples

blocks.text: Description
The u (unicode) flag enables full Unicode support in the regular expression.

By default, JavaScript and regex treats 4-byte Unicode characters
(like emojis or less common symbols) as two separate 2-byte "surrogate" code units.

The u flag treats the pattern as a sequence of Unicode code points, which is important for correctly
handling characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP).
RegExp y Modifier

blocks.caption: Examples
Examples

blocks.text: Description

The y (Sticky) flag performs a "sticky" search that matches only from the lastIndex
property of the RegExp object.

The y flag  ensures that subsequent matches start immediately
after the previous one, without skipping characters.
